Convert a climate data frame to a FINN environment array

Source: R/climateDF2array.R
climateDF2array.Rd

Reshapes a long-format climate table into the site x year x variable array FINN uses internally, auto-detecting the time resolution from the columns.

Usage

climateDF2array(climate_dt, env_vars)

Arguments

climate_dt

A data.frame/data.table of climate values in long format, with siteID, a time column (e.g. year), and one column per variable.

env_vars

character Names of the environmental variable columns to extract.

Value

A numeric array of environmental values indexed by site, time and variable: [site, year, variable] for a yearly table, [site, year, month, variable] with a month column and [site, year, month, day, variable] with a day column. Sites and years are in increasing order; the array has no dimnames, and the year axis holds only the years present in the table. A combination of siteID, year (and month, day where present) that appears more than once is an error, whether or not the rows are identical. Missing (siteID, year) combinations become NA in the array.

See also

finn_data for the env table of fit(), which is converted with this function

Examples

library(data.table)
# yearly climate of three sites over 22 years -> array [site, year, variable]
env <- fia_env_dt[siteID %in% 1:3]
a <- climateDF2array(env, env_vars = c("temp", "prec"))
dim(a)
#> [1]  3 22  2
head(a[1, , ])                # site 1; the rows are the years 1, 2, ...
#>          [,1] [,2]
#> [1,] 3.958333  547
#> [2,] 3.958333  547
#> [3,] 3.958333  547
#> [4,] 3.958333  547
#> [5,] 3.958333  547
#> [6,] 3.958333  547

# a monthly table (siteID, year, month) gives a fourth dimension of 12 months
monthly <- CJ(siteID = 1:2, year = 2001:2002, month = 1:12)
monthly[, temp := 10 + 8 * sin((month - 4) / 12 * 2 * pi)]
#> Key: <siteID, year, month>
